checks: Briefing a second agent, passes on all four limits the person set, including that the worker may not merge.
Scopes rules with a nested `AGENTS.md`, not `.claude/rules/`, so every agent sees them.
Moves a release procedure out of the root `AGENTS.md` and drops a file listing the code shows.
Asked to write down a rule a person stated in five words, does not add an exception, a reason, or a wider scope of its own, and names what to ask the person.

Designing a feed-refresh dispatcher whose refresh and retry intervals come from configuration stores the last success and failure times and computes due-ness in the query, not a stored next-attempt time.
Stops a no-deadline sweep's passes piling up by checking the queue before starting a pass, keeping the chain of capped jobs and its own position.
Makes an overlapping purge sweep safe with a re-check in the delete and a compare-and-set on its cursor, and takes no lock.
Writes a job that re-enqueues stuck exports on a table users also edit; finds and marks them by columns the export pipeline owns, never `updated_at`.
Asked by a review to guard a cursor row every run shares, gives each run its own position in job data and removes the shared write.
Flags a dispatcher predicate no index can serve and a job id keyed only by the entity.
Asks for one job per reconciler stage, with no shared budget, error list, or cursor map.
Reviews a session purge that locks a page plus one extra row; asks for one delete with the expiry re-checked and no lock, stops on a short page, and raises the per-row trigger and cascade.

Reviews a reindex sweep of profiles by `updated_at` in a repository where a trigger in the first migration bumps it; finds the trigger, takes the sweep off `updated_at`, and asks for an idempotent notification and a second-run test.

Writing a sweep that pushes unsynced invoices to a provider, backs off a failed invoice with a due time and retires it after a set number of attempts, so failing rows cannot hold the head of every run.
Reviewing retries around a payment call, says in shopper terms that a shopper can wait over a minute after "Pay now" and be charged twice.
Fixes a crashing report at the lookup that misses, not with a default value, and adds a test that fails without the fix.
Fixes an un-awaited write behind an intermittent test instead of adding a retry or a longer timeout.
Working unattended, takes the upgrade, the test location, and the dead-code check itself, and asks only about dropping a table, with a recommendation.
Groups updates by vendor or package family with a cooldown, not by version type, dependency type, or a catch-all.
Rebases a Dependabot pull request that carries a person's fix by hand, and does not ask Dependabot to rebuild it.
Sends the user to the web page that starts a Dependabot run, and invents no API call.
Asks for at least seven days on every ecosystem and semver key when a Dependabot workflow holds a write token.
Guard: adding a docs section about decisions made in a session states them as facts with their reasons, with no note of who made them.
Flags restated config values, history and plans in a README, and a comment that explains history.
Writes how to fetch changing numbers into a README section, not the numbers.
Answers two expected coupon failures without sending them to the error tracker, and still reports the rest.
Gives a new failure a code from one typed list of codes, and the client branches on the code, not the message.
Puts the order id and two amounts on the error as fields and keeps its message a fixed string.
Proposes a README, a history log, and an agent rules file for a new eval suite.

Logs a grader change and does not report a one-attempt rerun as an improvement.
Renames a column as add, write both, backfill, switch reads, and drop in later deploys, not in place.
Guard: accepts a mounted route behind an off flag that no page calls yet.
Defaults a new flag to off and reports deployed separately from enabled.
Asks for a registered entry point before a table and a service merge.
Reruns the generator on a conflicted generated API client and gives no hand-merged block to paste.
Lets pnpm merge a conflicted lockfile, takes neither side, and keeps the pre-push hook.

After a stacked branch's base is squash-merged, resolves the merge's conflicts hunk by hand instead of taking its own side, and removes a deleted file the merge brought back.
Stages the files of the fix by name and leaves unrelated and generated changes out.
Adding coverage reporting to a public repository's test job, uploads to Codecov in a step that cannot fail the job.
Asked to chain four independent jobs in series to save runner minutes, keeps the jobs that do not depend on each other in parallel.

Keeps `actions: write` out of any job that runs checked-out code.

Asked to fold 24 parallel shards into 4 jobs that each loop over six, keeps one shard to a job and at least 12 shards.
With the account at its limit, advises against rerunning a failed job to see whether it is flaky, and reads its log instead.
Says a move from Free to Team leaves the macOS limit at 5 and cuts the macOS jobs instead. Ceiling case.
Asked for a loop that polls a run until its jobs start, gives one query of the job timestamps and no loop.
Asked to cancel older runs on `main` with 11 jobs running on a plan that allows 60, says the account is under its limit and cancels nothing.

Asked to cancel whatever is superseded, cancels only the two older runs on a feature branch and keeps the newest one, the merge-queue run, and the runs on the default branch.

Checks that a months-old note still holds on the default branch before filing it.

Limits pull requests to collaborators and requires approval for every outside contributor's runs.

Says the OpenTofu provider has no attribute for two settings and gives the REST calls.
Adds a recovery path for permanently failed jobs beyond the dead-letter queue.
Returns 202 with a job id instead of waiting on the job inside the request.
Puts an outbox relay and a ledger write on a queue of their own, not a lane on the shared queue.
Asks a repair job to read database rows, not the queue's failed jobs, and for failed jobs not to be kept forever.
Gives a floodable webhook job family its own lane.
Uses resource paths, the public id, and hashed tokens.
Uses an edge-verified claim for cache bypass only, and lets the origin authorize.
Orders a new handler: authenticate, resolve the project in the URL, validate the body, then act.
Makes the slug the canonical route and permanently redirects old UUID links to it.
Asked to fix one crash, also fixes or reports the two sibling call sites with the same null dereference.

Caps an inbox read at 500 rows looked at and still tells the client to keep paging when the cap stops it short.
Guard: returns a banner's three latest sign-ins with one fixed-limit query and no cursor or next-page flag; has no skill-fired grader.
Asks for one walk over posts with the mute filter in the query, not a capped pool filtered afterward.
Fixes a slow inbox read by bounding the rows one request scans, and keeps the client paging from where the scan stopped.
Bounds a new tool's limit and day range, which the model supplies, through one shared helper.
Passes a fetched page to the model as delimited data, outside the system prompt, with an instruction not to follow it.
Takes the model for a new classifier from configuration or an argument, with no model id or fallback in the code.
Runs portable core tests once and asks for a written blocker before a web view.
Commits the project specification and ignores the generated Xcode project.
Ends a SwiftUI list and shows its empty state from the API's next-page flag, with the paging state outside the view.
Prepares a first publish for a person to run, and never publishes itself.
Sets up trusted publishing for an existing package without publishing or changing trust.

Adds dependencies with pnpm in the right fields and keeps the root export.
Names the affected unit tests, the browser spec, and the user-visible surfaces, not only code callers.

Checks redirects and metadata over plain HTTP and locates a button by role.

Removes duplication between three lookups by sharing the column list, and keeps each statement's name literal in its SQL.
Rechecks every query that depends on a changed index, found through the query builders.
Ships a new query with explicit columns, a bound, an operation-name comment, and its index.

Partitions by `RANGE` on the id with a default partition, not `HASH`.

References a generated id from other tables, not the customer's text code. Ceiling case.

Adds no `created_at DEFAULT now()` beside a UUIDv7 key.

Has a fake HTTP client answer by request path, not by a queue of replies in call order.
